item.title: LLM Benchmark Update: DeepSeek V4 Pro and OpenCode Harness Limitations
item.description:
LLM Benchmark Update: DeepSeek V4 Pro and OpenCode Harness Limitations

This update documents new developments in an autonomous coding benchmark repository, specifically addressing how OpenCode harness effects impact cross-model comparisons and the recent successful benchmarking of DeepSeek V4 Pro.

🔍 Overview

  • DeepSeek V4 Pro Benchmark: A new round (dated 2026-05-04) successfully measured DeepSeek V4 Pro using the deepclaude env-swap shim via Claude Code’s autonomous loop. This resolved a prior inability to measure the model caused by an opencode reasoning_content interop bug.
  • Harness Limitations: It was identified that opencode substring-matches model IDs to inject family-specific system prompts (e.g., bespoke prompts for Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi) versus a generic default for others (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM). Consequently, cross-family score differences may reflect prompt tuning rather than model capability.
  • Multi-Agent Strategy: An analysis (dated 2026-04-25) evaluated whether pairing a planner with a cheaper executor is cost-effective compared to using a solo Opus model.

⚙️ Key Details

The benchmark uses a fixed Rails application brief to compare local and cloud models. The current successful execution path involves a two-phase OpenRouter run:

  • Phase 1: Builds the Rails app.
  • Phase 2: Continues the same session to validate local boot, docker build, and docker compose up –build.

Current Model Rankings (0-100 Rubric)

Model Score Notes
Claude Opus 4.7 97 Benchmark leader; ~$1.10/run
GPT 5.4 xHigh 97 Ties Opus; ~$16/run (15x cost)
GPT 5.5 xHigh 96 40% cheaper and 20% faster than 5.4 (~$10/run)
Claude Opus 4.8 95 Newest Opus run; 34 tests, 16m48s
Kimi K2.6 87 Best value; ~$0.30/run
Claude Opus 4.6 83 Missing rescue around LLM calls
Gemini 3.1 Pro 82 Real Turbo Streams, cache-backed persistence

Evaluation Methodology

  • Rubric: Rankings are based on 8 dimensions including deliverables, RubyLLM correctness, tests, error handling, persistence, Hotwire, architecture, and production-readiness.
  • Metric Warning: File count and test count are considered misleading. For example, Kimi K2.5 wrote 37 tests but none mocked RubyLLM, while Gemini 3.1 Pro scored higher with only 11 tests due to correct signatures.
  • Hallucination Penalty: A “benchmark-killing pattern” occurs when models hallucinate APIs and then write tests that mock those hallucinations (e.g., DeepSeek V3.2 mocking a non-existent RubyLLM::Client.any_instance).

#LLMBenchmarks #DeepSeek #OpenCode #Claude #AIEngineering

Source: akitaonrails/llm-coding-benchmark

item.title: OpenCode AI Coding Agent Integrates with Open Weight Models on Amazon Bedrock
item.description:
OpenCode AI Coding Agent Integrates with Open Weight Models on Amazon Bedrock

OpenCode is an open source, terminal-native AI coding agent built in Go that now pairs with open weight models on Amazon Bedrock to provide a locally running assistant with secure cloud inference.

🧩 How it works

OpenCode manages coding tasks through the following capabilities:

  • Reads and edits files
  • Runs shell commands
  • Understands project structure using Language Server Protocol (LSP) diagnostics
  • Connects to over 75 LLM providers, including Amazon Bedrock

⚙️ Key details

Amazon Bedrock provides serverless access to open weight models where code, prompts, and responses remain within the user’s AWS account. The service does not use inputs or outputs to train foundation models.

Feature Detail
Compliance HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, and GDPR
Security Inherits IAM policies, CloudTrail logging, PrivateLink connectivity, and encryption controls
Scalability Default limits of 100M tokens per minute and 10K requests per minute
Model Switching Single API parameter change

Cost Tiers

  • Priority: For latency-sensitive production
  • Standard: On-demand inference (pay per token)
  • Flex: 50 percent lower cost for variable-latency workloads

🚀 Availability

Users can utilize specific models and profiles on Bedrock:

  • Kimi K3: A model that reasons before answering (depth set via reasoning_config as low, high, or max). It can be invoked via:
    • global.moonshotai.kimi-k3: A global profile routing requests worldwide, costing approximately 10% less than a geographic profile.
    • us.moonshotai.kimi-k3: A US geographic profile for data residency requirements.
  • Other Models: Practical examples include OpenAI GPT-OSS 120B and NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 120B.

💡 Why it matters

Recent industry reports and benchmarks highlight the shift toward open weight models and agentic workflows:

  • Adoption: According to McKinsey’s 2025 report, 76 percent of organizations expect to increase open source AI usage, and leading adopters are 40 percent more likely to use open weight models.
  • Performance: CrowdStrike’s fine-tuned NVIDIA Nemotron achieved 96% valid query accuracy, outperforming Claude Sonnet 4.5 (94%) and GPT-4o (61%).
  • Cost: Gartner’s 2026 analysis states agentic workflows multiply token consumption 5–30x, making cost-per-token critical.
  • Evaluation: The Artificial Analysis Coding Index benchmarks real-world tasks (SWE-Bench, Terminal-Bench, SWE-Atlas), and Amazon Bedrock Evaluations allows for side-by-side comparisons using human review, LLM-as-a-judge, or automatic scoring.

#OpenCode #AmazonBedrock #OpenSourceAI #AICodingAgent #AWS

Source: Use open weight models as your AI coding agent with Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services

item.title: OpenCode Go Offers $10/month Access to Reliable Open Coding Models
item.description:
OpenCode Go Offers $10/month Access to Reliable Open Coding Models

OpenCode has launched OpenCode Go, a $10‑per‑month subscription that provides reliable, low‑latency access to popular open‑source coding models.

🔍 Overview

  • Open models now perform close to proprietary models on coding tasks.
  • Reliable, low‑latency access to these models can be difficult because provider quality and availability vary.
  • OpenCode Go addresses this gap with a stable global service, especially for international users.

🧩 How it works

  • Subscribe to OpenCode Go and receive an API key.
  • The service functions like any other provider in the OpenCode platform.
  • It is optional; users can still use OpenCode without the subscription.
  • Designed for OpenCode and similar coding agents that send comparable request types.
  • Traffic is monitored to prevent abuse that could degrade other users’ experience.

⚙️ Key details

  • Pricing: $10 per month.
  • Usage limits are expressed as monthly dollar amounts; each model enforces:
    • 5‑hour limit: 20 % of the monthly limit
    • Weekly limit: 50 % of the monthly limit
    • Monthly limit: 100 % of the monthly limit
  • Token pricing is listed per 1 M tokens (exact amounts are model‑specific).
  • The list of available models may change as new models are tested and added.
  • The x‑opencode‑session header request remains open, but sending that header is no longer required.
  • Clients beyond OpenCode have been validated, though future support is not guaranteed and some have incomplete session support.

🚀 Availability

  • Subscription costs $10/month and provides stable global access.
  • Primarily aimed at international users seeking consistent performance.
  • Works with the latest version v0.81.6 or later, which includes the session‑header fix.

💡 Why it matters

  • Open models have improved to near‑proprietary performance, offering a cheaper alternative for coding tasks.
  • Because many providers can serve these models competitively, costs are generally lower than closed‑source options.
  • OpenCode Go bundles reliable, low‑latency access into a simple subscription, reducing the overhead of managing multiple providers.

#OpenCode #OpenSourceAI #CodingModels

Source: Go

item.title: OpenCode launches open source AI coding agent with desktop app
item.description:
OpenCode launches open source AI coding agent with desktop app

OpenCode, an open source coding agent, has released a new AI-powered development tool alongside a desktop application.

🔍 Overview

OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent designed to assist developers with coding tasks. It is available as both a command-line tool and a desktop application.

🧩 How it works

OpenCode includes two built-in agents that can be toggled with the Tab key:

  • build – A full-access agent for development work.
  • plan – A read-only agent for analysis and code exploration, which denies file edits by default and requests permission before running bash commands.

Additionally, OpenCode features a general subagent for complex searches and multistep tasks, invoked using @general in messages.

⚙️ Key details

  • Installation paths follow this priority order:

    1. $OPENCODE_INSTALL_DIR – Custom installation directory
    2. $XDG_BIN_DIR – XDG Base Directory Specification compliant path
    3. $HOME/bin – Standard user binary directory (if it exists or can be created)
    4. $HOME/.opencode/bin – Default fallback

  • Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

  • Download options:

    • Directly from the releases page
    • Via the official website: opencode.ai/download

🚀 Availability

  • OpenCode is available as an open source project.
  • Contributions are welcome; see the contributing docs for guidelines.
  • Users are asked to clarify in their project READMEs if their project name includes “opencode” but is not affiliated with the OpenCode team.

💡 Why it matters

OpenCode provides developers with an accessible, open source tool for AI-assisted coding, offering both development and analysis agents to streamline workflows.

#OpenCode #AIcoding #opensource #codingagent #desktopapp
